In this instalment of Stable Tours, TTR catches up with Queensland trainer Jack Bruce to discuss the proven, rejuvenated, tried performers who have helped establish his stable, alongside an exciting group of younger horses shaping its next chapter.

Jo McKinnon's entry into TTR's problems and solutions series highlighted the need to create better equestrians to take ownership of retired Thoroughbreds. How we can achieve this has several stages, but the common theme remains that this isn't a problem anyone can tackle alone.

A buoyant first day of selling at the Arqana August Yearling Sale was topped by a seven-figure son of Justify, who was the source of a protracted bidding battle between giants Godolphin and Coolmore. Stall Perlen dug deep to secure a Wootton Bassett colt and China Horse Club picked up a well-related filly.

Cosmic Crusader remained unbeaten in the east after completing the G3 Bletchingly Stakes-G2 PB Lawrence Stakes double at Caulfield, and Shadhavar rolled her rivals in her Listed Regal Roller Stakes resumption. At Rosehill, progressive mares Attractiveness and Eagle Express shape as stakes horses for their trainers, the latter helping Chris Waller achieve a quartet on the card.

The 3-year-olds were out in force on Saturday as spring fever swept over Caulfield, where Hard Kick bounced back to his best in the G3 Vain Stakes, and Rosehill, where Chilly Girl surged home to win the Listed Rosebud. Over in Ruakaka, She's No Saint became Prague's second stakes winner when taking out the G3 Northland Breeders' Stakes.

A strong Saturday of racing signals that early spring is in the air, with quality 3-year-olds taking centre stage across the country, as well as proven Weight-for-age campaigners that take aim at the G2 P.B Lawrence Stakes at Caulfield.

Three-time Group 1 winner Sir Delius again looked in excellent order winning one of the Group trials alongside Warwoven and Enriched on the Kensington, while a couple of 3-year-old winners also caught the eye in an action-packed morning of trials at Randwick.

In 2025/26, Godolphin changed their training model to distribute their horses across several stables and the experiment was a resounding success with 11 Group 1 races won. For this season, the promise of Anamoe’s first crop and with many of their stars remaining in work, they are striving towards a similar lofty goal.
